mcqs.prompt: A technician must recommend a filesystem for a new Windows server that needs per-file permissions, built-in encryption, and disk quotas for users. Which filesystem supports all three?
mcqs.context: A Windows server filesystem is needed with permissions, encryption, and quotas.

options.rationale: NTFS supports ACL permissions, EFS encryption, compression, and quotas — the full requirement set.
FAT32 has no permissions, encryption, or quotas, and caps files at 4 GB.
exFAT lifts the 4 GB file limit but has no permissions, encryption, or quotas.
ext4 is the Linux default filesystem, not native to Windows.

mcqs.explanation: NTFS provides ACL-based permissions, EFS file encryption, compression, and disk quotas — why it is the default for Windows system drives and servers.

mcqs.prompt: A user needs to move a 12 GB video file between a Windows PC and a macOS laptop using a USB flash drive. Which filesystem should the drive use so BOTH operating systems can read and write it?
mcqs.context: A flash drive must move a 12 GB file between Windows and macOS.

options.rationale: exFAT is natively readable/writable by both Windows and macOS and supports files larger than 4 GB — the right choice.
macOS can read NTFS but cannot natively write to it without extra software.
FAT32 works on both but has a 4 GB per-file limit, so the 12 GB video will not fit.
APFS is macOS-native; Windows cannot read it without third-party tools.

mcqs.explanation: exFAT is the cross-platform flash-drive format: both Windows and macOS read/write it natively, and it supports files beyond FAT32's 4 GB limit.

mcqs.prompt: A company discovers that a legacy Windows application stores its configuration in the registry and only runs on Windows. The IT team is evaluating Linux as a replacement platform. Which concern is MOST relevant?
mcqs.context: A Windows-only app with registry config is being evaluated against Linux migration.

options.rationale: Windows applications that depend on the registry and Windows APIs generally do not run natively on Linux — the primary migration concern.
Case sensitivity is a minor file-handling difference, not the main blocker.
Linux can read NTFS; the app itself is the problem.
Resolution support is not a migration blocker.

mcqs.explanation: OS compatibility is the key migration concern: registry-based Windows applications typically need Windows or a compatibility layer (Wine/VM) to run on Linux.

mcqs.prompt: A user's aging Windows 10 PC is still receiving security updates, but the manufacturer has stopped releasing new hardware drivers. Which term BEST describes this stage of the product lifecycle?
mcqs.context: An OS still gets security updates, but the vendor has stopped new hardware drivers.

options.rationale: The vendor stopped releasing new drivers — an update limitation that constrains support even while security patches continue.
EOL means NO more updates at all, including security patches; that is not yet the case here.
Compatibility mode is a Windows execution setting, not a lifecycle stage.
Multiboot is running multiple OSes; unrelated to lifecycle.

mcqs.explanation: Update limitations describe a product that still receives some updates (security) but no longer gets new features or drivers. EOL means all updates cease.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is installing Windows on a new PC that has an empty 3 TB drive and UEFI firmware. Which partition scheme should be used so the full capacity is available?
mcqs.context: A 3 TB drive with UEFI firmware needs a partition scheme supporting the full capacity.

options.rationale: GPT supports drives larger than 2 TB and is required for UEFI boot — the right scheme here.
MBR is limited to 2 TB and 4 primary partitions, so a 3 TB drive would lose capacity.
FAT32 is a filesystem, not a partition scheme.
APFS is a macOS filesystem.

mcqs.explanation: GPT (GUID Partition Table) supports disks over 2 TB and pairs with UEFI. MBR tops out at 2 TB and belongs with legacy BIOS.

mcqs.prompt: A user's Windows PC fails to boot after a failed update. The technician wants to fix the OS installation while keeping the user's files and applications. Which installation type accomplishes this?
mcqs.context: A failed update left Windows unbootable; files and apps must be preserved.

options.rationale: An in-place repair/upgrade reinstalls system files while preserving files, settings, and applications.
A clean install wipes the partition, losing files and applications.
Multiboot adds another OS; it does not repair the existing one.
A network (PXE) install deploys a fresh image, not a file-preserving repair.

mcqs.explanation: A repair installation (in-place upgrade from media) replaces Windows system files while keeping user data, settings, and apps. Clean installs erase everything.

mcqs.prompt: A company needs to deploy the same configured Windows image to 100 identical workstations. Which deployment method is MOST efficient?
mcqs.context: 100 identical workstations need the same Windows configuration.

options.rationale: Image deployment clones a prepared, configured image to many identical machines — the efficient choice.
Installing manually on 100 machines is slow and inconsistent.
Internet recovery reinstalls a stock OS, not the company configuration.
Multiboot configures multiple OSes on one machine; unrelated.

mcqs.explanation: Image deployment (e.g., with MDT/SCCM or third-party imaging) clones a golden image to many identical workstations quickly and consistently.

mcqs.prompt: Before upgrading a user's PC from Windows 10 to Windows 11, the technician runs a compatibility check and finds the PC lacks TPM 2.0. What is the significance of this finding?
mcqs.context: A Windows 11 upgrade check shows the PC lacks TPM 2.0.

options.text: The PC does not meet a Windows 11 hardware requirement
options.rationale: TPM 2.0 is a mandatory Windows 11 hardware requirement — the upgrade cannot proceed as-is.

options.text: The upgrade will run slower without TPM
options.rationale: TPM absence is a blocking requirement, not a performance issue.

options.text: The PC needs a larger drive instead
options.rationale: TPM is a security chip requirement, unrelated to drive size.

options.text: The technician should use a repair installation
options.rationale: Repair installations do not bypass hardware requirements.

mcqs.explanation: Windows 11 requires TPM 2.0 (plus a supported CPU, 4 GB RAM, and 64 GB storage). Without TPM 2.0, the machine cannot be upgraded to Windows 11.

mcqs.prompt: A small business wants to join its Windows PCs to a central domain for centralized user management. Which Windows edition supports joining an Active Directory domain?
mcqs.context: Windows PCs must join an Active Directory domain.

options.rationale: Windows Pro editions support domain join, BitLocker, and Group Policy — required for AD membership.
Windows Home cannot join an Active Directory domain.
N editions differ in media features, not domain support.
Windows Home editions do not support domain join.

mcqs.explanation: Windows Pro (and Enterprise) editions support domain join, BitLocker, RDP hosting, and gpedit. Home editions do not join Active Directory domains.

mcqs.prompt: A technician compares Windows editions for a user who needs full-disk encryption and Remote Desktop hosting on a work laptop. Which edition is the MINIMUM that provides both features?
mcqs.context: A work laptop needs BitLocker and Remote Desktop hosting.

options.rationale: Windows Pro includes BitLocker and can host Remote Desktop sessions — the minimum edition with both.
Windows Home lacks BitLocker and RDP hosting.
N editions are feature variants (no media player), not the edition determining BitLocker/RDP.
Windows SE is a classroom/education edition with limited features.

mcqs.explanation: BitLocker full-disk encryption and hosting Remote Desktop sessions require Windows Pro or better. Home editions can only connect TO remote desktops, not host them.

mcqs.prompt: A user reports that an application launches automatically every time they sign in to Windows, and they want to stop it. Which tool should the technician use?
mcqs.context: An app auto-launches at sign-in and must be disabled.

options.rationale: Task Manager's Startup tab lists and disables sign-in apps — the modern location for this setting.
Event Viewer shows logs, not startup apps.
Disk Management handles partitions.
Certificate Manager manages certificates, not startup entries.

mcqs.explanation: Task Manager > Startup shows every sign-in application with its impact and a Disable button — the current Windows way to manage startup apps (msconfig's Startup tab is legacy).

mcqs.prompt: A technician needs to shrink a partition and create a new one for a second OS. Which administrative tool performs partition management?
mcqs.context: A partition must be shrunk and a new partition created.

options.rationale: Disk Management shrinks, extends, formats, and creates partitions.
Device Manager handles drivers and hardware.
Task Scheduler runs scheduled tasks.
Resource Monitor shows live system resource usage.

mcqs.explanation: Disk Management (diskmgmt.msc) is the MMC snap-in for partition operations: shrink, extend, create, format, and assign drive letters.

mcqs.prompt: A Windows device shows a yellow exclamation mark next to an unknown device in Device Manager. What does this indicate?
mcqs.context: An unknown device shows a yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager.

options.text: The device has a driver problem
options.rationale: A yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager means the device is not working properly, usually a driver issue.

options.text: The device is disabled by policy
options.rationale: A down-arrow icon indicates a disabled device; the exclamation mark means a driver problem.
Working devices show no warning icon.

options.text: The device needs a firmware update
options.rationale: Firmware updates are not indicated by the exclamation mark.

mcqs.explanation: In Device Manager, a yellow exclamation mark (or question mark for unknown devices) indicates a driver or configuration problem. A disabled device shows a downward arrow.

mcqs.prompt: A school district is choosing a Windows edition for student laptops that will run only store-provided apps and cannot install arbitrary desktop software. Which edition is designed for this locked-down education scenario?
mcqs.context: Student laptops need a locked-down Windows edition that only runs Store apps.

options.rationale: Windows 11 SE is the education edition that runs only approved apps from the Store — built for locked-down student devices.
Pro is the full business edition with unrestricted desktop app installation.
N editions omit media features; they do not restrict app installation.
Enterprise is a full-featured volume edition, not app-restricted.

mcqs.explanation: Windows 11 SE (and the older Windows 10 S mode) restrict installation to Store apps, ideal for managed student devices. Pro/Enterprise/N editions allow traditional desktop software.

mcqs.prompt: A user's web browsing works but their PC cannot resolve new hostnames. The technician wants to clear the cached name-resolution records. Which command accomplishes this?
mcqs.context: Hostname resolution is failing; the DNS cache needs clearing.

options.rationale: ipconfig /flushdns clears the local DNS resolver cache — the fix for stale name records.
Releasing the DHCP lease drops the IP address; unrelated to DNS cache.
netstat lists connections and ports.
gpupdate refreshes Group Policy, not DNS.

mcqs.explanation: ipconfig /flushdns clears the DNS resolver cache, fixing stale or corrupted name resolutions. /release and /renew manage the DHCP lease.

mcqs.prompt: A technician needs to verify which TCP ports are currently listening on a Windows server. Which command shows active connections and listening ports?
mcqs.context: Listening TCP ports on a Windows server must be identified.

options.rationale: netstat displays active connections and listening ports with their state.
ping tests reachability; it does not list ports.
chkdsk checks disk integrity.
winver shows the Windows version.

mcqs.explanation: netstat (e.g., netstat -an) lists listening and established TCP/UDP endpoints, identifying which services are bound to which ports.

mcqs.prompt: Windows reports that protected system files are corrupted and some applications fail. Which TWO commands should the technician run, in order, to repair the system image and system files?
mcqs.context: Corrupted protected system files need repair.

options.rationale: DISM repairs the Windows system image that sfc relies on — run it first when the image is damaged.
sfc /scannow verifies and repairs protected system files using the repaired image.
chkdsk checks disk integrity, not system files.
diskpart manages partitions.
Formatting destroys the system; never a repair step.

mcqs.explanation: The correct repair sequence is DISM to restore the component store/image first, then sfc /scannow to repair system files against it. chkdsk handles disk errors, not file corruption.

mcqs.prompt: A technician needs to map a network share on a file server to the drive letter S: for a user. Which command maps a network drive?
mcqs.context: A network share must be mapped to drive letter S:.

options.rationale: net use maps a network share to a drive letter — the command for this task.
robocopy copies files; it does not map drives.
nslookup queries DNS.
pathping traces routes with latency stats.

mcqs.explanation: net use maps network shares to drive letters (e.g., net use S: \\server\share). robocopy is a file-copy tool; nslookup and pathping are network diagnostics.

mcqs.prompt: A user wants the OS to remember their session and start quickly after shutdown, but they sometimes need a full power-off for hardware changes. Which two power options address these needs?
mcqs.context: A user wants fast startup but also occasional full shutdowns.

options.rationale: Fast startup hibernates the kernel so the PC boots quickly after shutdown.
A Shift+Shut-down performs a full shutdown, clearing the hibernated kernel — needed for hardware changes.
Hibernate saves the session to disk for later resume, but does not give a full power-off.
USB selective suspend powers down idle USB devices; unrelated to boot speed.
Screen timeout turns off the display, not the system.

mcqs.explanation: Fast startup gives quick boots via kernel hibernation; a Shift+Shut-down performs a true full shutdown when needed (e.g., before hardware work). Hibernate and USB selective suspend are different power features.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is configuring File Explorer on a shared PC to reduce the risk of users double-clicking dangerous attachments. Which TWO File Explorer options support this goal?
mcqs.context: File Explorer settings should reduce dangerous-file risk on a shared PC.

options.text: Show file extensions for known file types
options.rationale: Visible extensions help users spot dangerous double-extension files (e.g., .pdf.exe).
Revealing hidden files helps users notice hidden malware files in folders.

options.text: Hide file extensions for known file types
options.rationale: Hiding extensions hides the .exe in .pdf.exe — the opposite of the goal.
The Recycle Bin is unrelated to file-extension visibility.
Hiding protected OS files conceals system files; it does not reveal extensions.

mcqs.explanation: Showing extensions (so .pdf.exe is visible) and showing hidden files (so hidden malware is visible) reduce the risk of opening dangerous files. Hiding extensions does the opposite.

mcqs.prompt: A user's laptop does not respond when the lid is closed and wants it to sleep automatically. Where is this configured?
mcqs.context: The laptop lid-closing action needs to be set to sleep.

options.text: Power Options (Choose what closing the lid does)
options.rationale: Power Options includes the lid-closing action setting — the correct configuration location.
Sound settings manage audio devices.
Mail settings configure email accounts.
Gaming settings configure game bar and modes.

mcqs.explanation: Power Options > Choose what closing the lid does sets the lid action (sleep, hibernate, shut down, do nothing) for battery and plugged-in modes.

mcqs.prompt: A technician needs to uninstall a legacy application that does not appear in the Settings > Apps list. Which alternative tool can remove it?
mcqs.context: A legacy app must be uninstalled but does not appear in Settings > Apps.

options.rationale: Programs and Features lists traditional (Win32) installed programs — legacy apps often appear here even when missing from Settings > Apps.
Device Manager manages hardware, not installed software.
Event Viewer shows logs.
Task Scheduler runs scheduled tasks.

mcqs.explanation: Programs and Features (Control Panel) lists traditional Win32 applications; some legacy apps only appear there, not in the newer Settings > Apps page.

mcqs.prompt: A technician explains Windows network profiles to a user who travels with a laptop. Which TWO statements about Public vs Private network profiles are correct?
mcqs.context: Windows Public vs Private network profile behavior is being explained.

options.text: Public profiles block file and printer sharing by default
options.rationale: The Public profile is the most restrictive — discovery and sharing are off.

options.text: Private profiles allow file sharing and device discovery
options.rationale: Private is for trusted networks (home/office) where sharing is permitted.

options.text: Public profiles are used only on domain networks
options.rationale: Domain networks use the Domain profile; Public is for untrusted networks like coffee-shop Wi-Fi.

options.text: Private profiles disable the firewall entirely
options.rationale: The firewall stays on for every profile; rules differ, not the firewall itself.

options.text: Profiles have no effect on firewall rules
options.rationale: Each profile carries its own firewall rule set — that is the entire point of profiles.

mcqs.explanation: Public = restrictive (no sharing/discovery) for untrusted networks; Private = permissive for trusted LANs; Domain is for AD networks. The firewall remains on in all profiles.

mcqs.prompt: A user's PC is a member of a workgroup. What does this imply about authentication?
mcqs.context: A PC in a workgroup needs local authentication.

options.text: Each PC maintains its own local user accounts
options.rationale: Workgroups are peer-to-peer: every PC has its own local accounts and there is no central directory.

options.text: Accounts are centralized in Active Directory
options.rationale: Centralized AD accounts are a domain feature, not a workgroup.

options.text: Group Policy is applied from a domain controller
options.rationale: Group Policy from domain controllers requires domain membership.

options.text: SSO works across all workgroup PCs
options.rationale: Workgroups have no single sign-on; each machine has separate credentials.

mcqs.explanation: In a workgroup, each PC has its own local user database — no central authentication. Domains centralize accounts in Active Directory with Group Policy and SSO.

mcqs.prompt: A remote user needs secure access to internal resources and will authenticate with a company-issued smart card. Which TWO technologies are involved?
mcqs.context: A remote user needs secure, smart-card-authenticated access to internal resources.

options.rationale: A VPN creates the encrypted tunnel for secure remote access to internal resources.
Smart cards authenticate via certificates — the credential the user presents.
Workgroups provide no centralized secure remote access.
MAC filtering is a wireless access control, not remote-access authentication.
APIPA is link-local addressing; unrelated.

mcqs.explanation: Remote secure access combines a VPN tunnel with strong authentication — here, certificate-based smart card authentication (e.g., 802.1X or VPN certificate auth).

mcqs.prompt: A macOS user needs to back up the entire system automatically to an external drive. Which built-in tool provides scheduled full-system backups?
mcqs.context: Automatic full-system backups on macOS to an external drive.

options.rationale: Time Machine automatically backs up the Mac to an external drive with hourly snapshots.
Disk Utility formats and repairs disks; it does not back up.
Keychain stores passwords and certificates.
Mission Control manages windows and desktops.

mcqs.explanation: Time Machine is macOS's built-in automatic backup tool, keeping hourly, daily, and weekly snapshots on an external drive.

mcqs.prompt: A Mac user wants to find which application is consuming the most CPU. Which built-in tool shows live process resource usage?
mcqs.context: The CPU-hungry application on a Mac must be identified.

options.rationale: Activity Monitor shows live CPU, memory, energy, disk, and network usage per process — the macOS equivalent of Task Manager.
Finder is the file manager.
Spotlight is search.
Gatekeeper controls app installation security.

mcqs.explanation: Activity Monitor displays per-process CPU/memory usage on macOS, letting users find and quit resource hogs.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is helping a macOS user install an application downloaded from the internet, but macOS refuses to open it, citing an unidentified developer. Which feature is blocking the app?
mcqs.context: macOS blocks an app from an unidentified developer.

options.rationale: Gatekeeper enforces app signing and notarization checks, blocking unsigned/unidentified-developer apps.
Time Machine is backups.
Keychain stores credentials.
Spotlight is search.

mcqs.explanation: Gatekeeper blocks apps not signed by an identified developer (or not notarized); users can override via right-click > Open or Security settings when they trust the source.

mcqs.prompt: A Linux administrator needs to change the permissions of a script so the owner can read/write/execute, the group can read/execute, and others have no access. Which chmod value achieves this?
mcqs.context: A script needs 750-style permissions: owner rwx, group r-x, others none.

options.rationale: 750 = owner rwx (7), group r-x (5), others none (0) — exactly the required permissions.
755 gives others read/execute; here others need no access.
700 gives the group no access; the group needs read/execute.
777 grants everyone full access — far too permissive.

mcqs.explanation: chmod numeric modes: 7=rwx, 5=r-x, 0=---. 750 grants owner rwx, group r-x, others none — the correct minimal permissions.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is following a Linux guide that says to install a package using the system's package manager on a Debian-based distribution. Which command installs a package on Debian/Ubuntu?
mcqs.context: A package must be installed on Debian/Ubuntu Linux.

options.rationale: apt is the Debian/Ubuntu package manager; sudo grants the needed admin rights.
dnf is the Red Hat/Fedora package manager, not Debian.
chmod changes permissions; it does not install packages.
grep searches file contents; unrelated to installation.

mcqs.explanation: apt (with sudo) installs packages on Debian/Ubuntu. dnf/yum serve Red Hat-family distributions; chmod and grep do unrelated tasks.

mcqs.prompt: A Linux user needs to find every line containing the word 'ERROR' inside a large log file. Which command-line tool filters lines by pattern?
mcqs.context: Lines containing 'ERROR' must be found in a log file.

options.rationale: grep searches files for lines matching a pattern — the standard log-filtering tool.
ls lists directory contents.
chmod changes file permissions.
df reports disk space usage.

mcqs.explanation: grep 'ERROR' /var/log/app.log prints matching lines. ls, chmod, and df serve listing, permissions, and disk-space tasks.

mcqs.prompt: A Linux technician needs to see how much free space remains on the root filesystem. Which command reports disk usage by filesystem?
mcqs.context: Free space on the root filesystem must be checked.

options.rationale: df -h reports filesystem disk usage in human-readable sizes — the right command.
ps lists running processes.
top shows live process/resource monitoring.
whoami prints the current user.

mcqs.explanation: df -h shows mounted filesystems with used/available space. ps/top monitor processes; whoami shows the current user.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is installing a 32-bit legacy application on a 64-bit Windows 11 PC. Which consideration is MOST important?
mcqs.context: A 32-bit legacy app is being installed on 64-bit Windows 11.

options.text: 32-bit apps generally run on 64-bit Windows via WOW64 compatibility
options.rationale: Windows runs 32-bit apps on 64-bit systems through WOW64 — the app will typically install and run.

options.text: The PC must be reinstalled with 32-bit Windows
options.rationale: No — 64-bit Windows runs 32-bit applications natively via WOW64.

options.text: The app needs a new filesystem
options.rationale: Filesystems are unrelated to 32/64-bit app compatibility.

options.text: The technician must enable Secure Boot first
options.rationale: Secure Boot affects booting, not application execution.

mcqs.explanation: 64-bit Windows includes WOW64, running 32-bit applications without reinstallation. Compatibility problems usually come from the app's OS version, not the bitness.

mcqs.prompt: A Windows installer triggers a UAC prompt asking for administrator permission. What does granting it allow the installer to do?
mcqs.context: A UAC prompt asks for admin permission during installation.

options.text: Make system-wide changes with elevated privileges
options.rationale: Granting the UAC prompt elevates the installer so it can write to protected system locations and install for all users.
UAC elevation grants admin rights for that process only, not a security bypass.
Elevation does not disable security features.
UAC has nothing to do with hardware requirements.

mcqs.explanation: UAC prompts elevate a single process to administrator so it can modify system areas. Denying it restricts the installer to per-user scope.

mcqs.prompt: A technician installs an application from the Microsoft Store on a Windows PC. Which TWO characteristics apply to Store apps?
mcqs.context: Installing an app from the Microsoft Store.

options.text: They install per-user without a separate installer wizard
options.rationale: Store apps install in a sandboxed per-user container without traditional setup wizards.

options.text: They receive automatic updates from the Store
options.rationale: Store apps update automatically through the Store — a key management benefit.
Store apps do not install drivers.
Store apps can be uninstalled from Settings > Apps.

options.text: They always require an MSI installer
options.rationale: Store apps use the APPX/MSIX packaging, not MSI.

mcqs.explanation: Microsoft Store apps install per-user, update automatically, and use APPX/MSIX packaging. They are uninstallable and do not install drivers or use MSI installers.

mcqs.prompt: A sales team collaborates on a spreadsheet simultaneously from different offices, with changes syncing instantly. Which type of tool provides this capability?
mcqs.context: A spreadsheet must support real-time multi-user collaboration.

options.text: Cloud productivity suite (e.g., Google Sheets / Microsoft 365)
options.rationale: Cloud productivity suites provide real-time co-editing, version history, and instant sync.

options.text: Local office suite with manual file sharing
options.rationale: Local suites require manual file transfers and do not co-edit in real time.
A print server shares printers, not documents.
An installer deploys software; it does not enable collaboration.

mcqs.explanation: Cloud productivity tools (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365) offer real-time collaboration, version history, and cloud sync — the described capability.

mcqs.prompt: A user edits a document on their phone while commuting, then opens the same document on their desktop and sees the changes. Which feature of cloud storage makes this possible?
mcqs.context: Edits made on a phone appear on the desktop document.

options.rationale: Cloud storage syncs files across devices automatically, so edits propagate to every signed-in device.
Partitioning divides a drive; unrelated.
Spooling queues print jobs.
Defragmentation optimizes drive layout.

mcqs.explanation: Cloud file sync (OneDrive, Google Drive, iCloud Drive) keeps files current across devices — edit on one device, see it on all.

mcqs.prompt: A company needs employees to share a document with an external contractor for VIEWING ONLY. Which cloud-sharing permission should be applied?
mcqs.context: An external contractor should view a shared document without editing.

options.rationale: A view-only share grants read access, preventing edits — the correct permission.
Edit access lets the contractor modify the document.
Transferring ownership gives full control.
Unrestricted publishing exposes the document broadly.

mcqs.explanation: Cloud sharing supports granular permissions; a view-only link lets external users read without editing. Least privilege dictates read-only for viewing.

mcqs.prompt: A macOS user cannot remember their saved Wi-Fi passwords and wants to review them. Which built-in tool stores and displays saved credentials?
mcqs.context: Saved Wi-Fi passwords must be reviewed on macOS.

options.rationale: Keychain Access stores and displays saved passwords, certificates, and Wi-Fi credentials.
Activity Monitor shows process resource usage.
Disk Utility manages disks.
Finder is the file manager.

mcqs.explanation: Keychain Access is the macOS credential store — passwords, certificates, and Wi-Fi network keys can be viewed (with the user's login password).

mcqs.prompt: A technician needs to check whether a remote server is reachable and measure round-trip time. Which command-line tool sends ICMP echo requests?
mcqs.context: Remote server reachability and round-trip time must be tested.

options.rationale: ping sends ICMP echo requests and reports round-trip times and packet loss — the reachability tool.
nslookup queries DNS records.
diskpart manages disk partitions.
robocopy copies files.

mcqs.explanation: ping tests reachability via ICMP echo and measures latency/loss. nslookup handles DNS; diskpart and robocopy serve storage and file tasks.

mcqs.prompt: An administrator needs to schedule a script to run every night at 2 AM on a Windows server. Which tool schedules tasks?
mcqs.context: A nightly 2 AM script run must be scheduled on Windows.

options.rationale: Task Scheduler creates and manages scheduled tasks with triggers like daily time — the right tool.
Performance Monitor tracks system counters.
Event Viewer shows logs.
Registry Editor edits configuration keys, not schedules.

mcqs.explanation: Task Scheduler (taskschd.msc) runs scripts and programs on triggers (time, event, logon). Performance Monitor, Event Viewer, and regedit serve other purposes.

mcqs.prompt: A technician is comparing Windows 10 and Windows 11 for a new deployment. Which difference is a characteristic of Windows 11?
mcqs.context: Windows 11 deployment characteristics are being reviewed.

options.text: Centered Start menu and rounded window corners
options.rationale: Windows 11 introduced the centered Start menu, rounded corners, and a redesigned taskbar.

options.text: The Start menu is always on the left with live tiles
options.rationale: Live tiles and the left-aligned Start menu are Windows 10 characteristics.

options.text: It requires only 2 GB of RAM
options.rationale: Windows 11 requires 4 GB minimum.
Windows 11 is 64-bit only.

mcqs.explanation: Windows 11's UI changes include the centered Start menu, rounded corners, and Snap Layouts. Windows 10 has left-aligned Start with live tiles; Windows 11 needs 4 GB RAM and is 64-bit only.
